title: The engine runs segmentation, uplift and ranking (16.15 phase B)
request: Phase B of 16.15: segmentation, uplift and ranking run in the engine through the same five stages, the holdout locked in the data stage, the choice made on validation, the holdout read once in the final stage; their libraries split into choose and score.
spec: Each kind brings its own machine; changing only the holdout's outcomes leaves every stage before the final identical; exports refuse; the Solution checks each kind's fields; acceptance in the engine for each kind.
plan: Split each library into a validation step and a scoring step whose composition is the old evaluate, its output unchanged.
Write the three machines with their locks and their engine acceptance.
Let the Solution, the card and the journeys take the three kinds.
Test that the holdout's outcomes reach only the final stage, for each kind.
Review, plant faults, measure the journeys, the harness suite and the workflow comparison.

decisions.decision: Segmentation's holdout number is the held-out rows' silhouette against data with no groups; the training stability is shown beside it.
decisions.why: A number computed on the training rows must never be reported as a holdout result.

decisions.decision: Segmentation's final stage scales every row with the training rows' fit.
decisions.why: A scaling fitted on all rows learns from the held-out rows.

decisions.decision: Uplift's validation builds outcomes for the training rows only, even where the models would not read the rest.
decisions.why: Code that cannot read the holdout cannot leak it after a later change.

decisions.decision: Ranking's outcome said in words counts with a table: it is an event in the window, not a column of the log.
decisions.why: A ranking problem has no outcome column, and its card would otherwise stay undefined.

decisions.decision: The sealed journeys keep expecting a refusal for the three kinds and the docstring says so.
decisions.why: The sealed set runs once; it is never edited to follow a change.

change: dclab_core uplift, ranking, segment and card with its changelog (0.35.0); dclab_rnd/kinds uplift, ranking and segmentation with capability.json; the journeys' harness and dev journeys; tests/test_kind_engine_library.py (new) and the engine, kind matrix, journeys and uplift tests; journeys JRN-003, harness HRN-002, workflow DWF-004; the playbook and the roadmap.

findings.defect: Ranking's problem card had no outcome.
findings.scenario: A ranking brief with a log and an items table stayed undefined on its outcome and the journey could not build.
findings.cause: The card counted an outcome only for kinds whose outcome is a table, not an event in a window.
findings.fix: Ranking's outcome said in words counts as defined.

findings.defect: The journeys' harness saved segmentation with a classification task.
findings.scenario: A segmentation journey built a project the engine refused, for a target it does not have.
findings.cause: The harness used one default task for every kind.
findings.fix: The stated kind's own base task is used.

findings.defect: Three tests still expected the three kinds to be refused.
findings.scenario: The kind matrix, the engine and the journeys' tests failed once the kinds ran in the engine.
findings.cause: They were written when the kinds were library only.
findings.fix: Each test now patches the kind to library only where it checks the refusal.

findings.defect: Segmentation's final stage fitted its scaling on every row.
findings.scenario: Changing a held-out row's values moved the scaling the training rows were placed with.
findings.cause: The final stage prepared the whole table.
findings.fix: The scaling is fitted on the training rows and applied to every row with segment.transform.

findings.defect: Segmentation's holdout number was a training number.
findings.scenario: The stability of the training rows' resamples was reported as the holdout metric.
findings.fix: The held-out rows' silhouette, against data with no groups, is the holdout number.

findings.defect: Uplift's interval was called 95% when it was the 90% one.
findings.scenario: The project's holdout interval read narrower than it is.
findings.cause: The library kept only a 90% interval.
findings.fix: A 95% interval is computed and named as such.

findings.defect: Uplift's overlap check read forbidden columns.
findings.scenario: A column the person forbade could decide whether the arms overlap.
findings.cause: The check took every candidate column.
findings.fix: Forbidden, identifier and moment columns are left out of it.

findings.defect: The readers every kind shares were untested on the three kinds.
findings.scenario: An export, the compact record, the answers or the report could break on a new machine unseen.
findings.fix: A shared test class checks every reader on each kind.

findings.defect: The sealed journeys' expectations were unstated.
findings.scenario: A reader would take their expected refusal as a defect.
findings.fix: The journeys' docstring says the sealed journeys still expect a refusal.

findings.defect: A planted scaling fitted on every row passed the tests.
findings.scenario: Segmentation's final stage preparing the whole table left every test green.
findings.cause: The tests compared numbers rounded beyond the change.
findings.fix: A test watches the rows the final stage fits its scaling on.

findings.defect: A card ignoring ranking's outcome in words passed the tests.
findings.scenario: Removing the event outcome from the card left every test green.
findings.cause: Only the journeys reached it, and they passed without it.

measurements.name: acceptance in the engine
measurements.gate: each kind passes its acceptance in the engine
measurements.result: uplift 12 of 12, ranking 12 of 12, segmentation 12 of 12; uplift_tree chosen on 3500 validation rows with a Qini of 0.0107 on 6000 held-out rows; the ranker's gain over popularity 0.0474; held-out silhouette 0.49 against 0.269 with no groups
measurements.against_gate: every check of each kind passed
limits: Invented replicas, one seed each in the matrix.

measurements.name: journeys
measurements.gate: the dev journeys still pass with the three kinds built
measurements.result: 15 of 15 dev journeys right, the three kinds now built to their holdout number
limits: One journey per kind; written by the developer.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: every planted fault caught or shown equivalent
measurements.result: 14 planted: 12 caught, 2 equivalent (code reading rows it then never uses)
measurements.against_gate: no fault missed that changes behaviour

measurements.name: workflow comparison
measurements.gate: the decision models in the workflow measured again on the changed journeys
measurements.result: the rules 15 of 15; the leakage classifier acting alone 14 of 15, with its check 15 of 15, as before
measurements.against_gate: the same verdict as the earlier runs

outcome: Segmentation, uplift and ranking run in the engine with their holdouts locked and read once; every kind but images now runs there.
lessons: A number on the training rows reported as the holdout is a leak of meaning, not of data.
A test that rounds can hide a fit made on the wrong rows: watch what the code reads.
A planted fault that survives may be equivalent; say why, or write the test.
risks: The sealed journeys still expect refusals for these kinds.
